## Summary

Ensure the herdr audit-freshness predicate enforces the canonical "at-or-near"
semantics and is the **single source of truth** shared by both the icon display
and the downtime (audit-dispatch) worker.

Audit freshness currently lives only in `isAuditFresh()` in
`packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`. It is the basis for the icon display
(`auditIcon` in `icons.ts`) AND is the documented freshness gate reused by the
downtime dispatch audit tier (`selectAuditCandidate` /
`getNextAuditCandidate` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, which
treats `!isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` as "needs a fresh `/skill:audit`").

Running an audit itself bumps the work item's `updatedAt` to within a fraction
of a second of its `auditedAt` (`wl audit-set` + `wl update --audit-text` +
the verdict-driven status transition). A freshness rule that requires a strict
gap on one side (e.g. only `auditedAt` comfortably ahead of `updatedAt`) can
therefore disagree with the just-persisted state. The canonical fix in
SorraAgents (SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4) treats an audit as fresh when its
`auditedAt` is **at or near** the item's `updatedAt` (within a small
tolerance) because a near-simultaneous `updatedAt` bump is the audit's own
persistence write.

This item makes ContextHub's herdr audit-freshness logic follow the same
at-or-near rule so the icon display and the downtime dispatcher agree, and
never disagree on a just-persisted audit.

## Expected behaviour

- `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` returns true (fresh) when `auditedAt`
  is at-or-near `updatedAt` within a small, named tolerance (the audit's own
  persistence write), and false otherwise.
- The icon (`auditIcon` in `icons.ts`) shows the fresh icon for a
  just-persisted audit (no longer shows the stale glyph for an audit the run
  just persisted).
- The downtime audit candidate selection (`selectAuditCandidate` /
  `getNextAuditCandidate` in `downtime-worker.ts`) uses the SAME
  `isAuditFresh` predicate, so a just-persisted fresh audit is NOT a dispatch
  candidate (no redundant `/skill:audit` re-run).
- Only one freshness definition exists; neither consumer re-implements its
  own comparison.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `isAuditFresh` in `icons.ts` treats `auditedAt` at-or-near `updatedAt`
   (within a documented tolerance constant) as fresh, covering the
   audit-persistence case (`auditedAt ~ updatedAt`, delta well under the
   tolerance).
2. A unit test asserts `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` is true for a
   just-persisted audit (auditedAt and updatedAt differ by milliseconds).
3. A unit test asserts a genuinely stale audit (item updated well after the
   audit) is still false (stale), unchanged.
4. `selectAuditCandidate` / `getNextAuditCandidate` in `downtime-worker.ts`
   continue to use the imported `isAuditFresh` as the sole filter; a
   just-persisted fresh item is excluded from candidates.
5. Both consumers import the same helper; no competing freshness comparison
   is introduced in the dispatch or icon paths.

## Notes / Open questions

- `isAuditFresh` currently hard-codes a magic `60000` ms literal. Prefer
  naming a constant (e.g. `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS`) and routing
  both consumers through it.
- Reconcile the comparison shape of `isAuditFresh` (`auditTime > updateTime -
  buffer`) with the canonical at-or-near semantics from the SorraAgents fix so
  both projects express the same intent. Confirm the target semantics with the
  operator before implementing.

## References

- discovered-from: SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4 (SorraAgents audit_runner child
  freshness at-or-near fix) — canonical reference implementation.
- related-to: WL-0MSI9FK2Q0074C31 (Audit candidate selection),
  WL-0MSI9WPNI0044R (Audit dispatch tier), parent WL-0MSI8H3HP700K0RG.
data.title: Unify audit-freshness at-or-near logic across icon display and downtime dispatcher

Mechanism under investigation: wl update --needs-producer-review bumps updatedAt (packages/shared/src/database.ts update()); herdr's isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt) (packages/herdr/src/icons.ts) then reports stale, which (a) degrades the TUI audit icon and (b) re-selects the item for audit-tier dispatch (selectAuditCandidate, packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts).

# counts in Herdr selection list are incorrect (WL-0MT26TE72002FLKX)

## Problem statement

The Herdr selection list header over-counts displayed items because it counts heading rows as work items. In the reported case the header shows "24 item(s) (top 24 of 100)" while the sum of group heading counts (19 in_review + 1 Critical Group 1 + 1 Critical Group 2 = 21 items) is correct — the 3 heading rows inflate the header to 24.

## Users

- **Herdr pane operator** — relies on the header count and "top N of M" badge to understand how many items are shown vs how many exist.
- **Producer triaging the backlog** — uses group heading counts and the header total to judge queue size.

Example user stories:
- As an operator viewing the Herdr list, I want the header "N item(s)" and "top N of M" to reflect the number of work items (not heading rows), so the counts reconcile with the group totals.
- As a producer, I want collapsed groups to still be counted correctly in the header, so hiding a group does not change the meaning of the total.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Header item count excludes heading rows** — With `displayRows` containing headings + items, the header renders `N = count of WorkItem rows` (not `displayRows.length`). For the reported fixture (21 items across 3 groups + 3 heading rows), the header shows "21 item(s)" instead of "24 item(s)".
2. **"top N of M" badge is correct** — When `totalActionableCount` is defined and `M > N`, the header shows `(top N of M)` where `N` is the WorkItem count above. No badge when `M <= N` or undefined. Truncated-window cases (e.g. `browseItemCount` limit) still show the correct `N`.
3. **Group heading counts unchanged and still correct** — Heading rows continue to show `count = top-level items in the group in the current view (post stage-filter)` and are unaffected by the header fix. Collapsed groups remain visible as headings but their hidden items are still counted in the header total.
4. **No regression in list chrome / layout** — Header truncation to `cols`, fold indicators, dynamic layout, filter label, and pane states (paused / code-freeze banners / auto-refresh) continue to behave as before; `rows - 1` pane invariant preserved.
5. **Documentation and tests updated** — Relevant doc/comment near the header derivation notes that `totalItems` is item count not row count; existing heading-rows / worklist renderer tests pass and a new or updated test asserts the heading-vs-item distinction. Full project test suite must pass; CHANGELOG.md excluded.

## Constraints

- Zero npm deps for herdr unless required; keep change surgical to header derivation and any count plumbing.
- Do not change ranking/selection order (`fetchNextItems` / `smart-selection` / `grouping`) — only what is counted for display.
- Preserve `totalActionableCount` semantics (actionable = `wl list --status open,in-progress,blocked` count via `fetchActionableCount`); fix counting, not the fetcher count source, unless clearly wrong.
- Keep heading rows first-class in `DisplayRow[]` for navigation/scroll/layout; only the count metric changes.

## Existing state

- **Header derivation:** `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts:3225` sets `const totalItems = displayRows.length` with comment "displayRows includes heading rows, so the item count shown is the row count — the same metric the header has always shown for the flattened list." The `totalCount` badge is `if (totalCount !== undefined && totalCount > totalItems) header += (top totalItems of totalCount)` — both sides are row counts, so headings inflate `totalItems` and the comparison.
- **Heading counts:** `WorkItemListState.getDisplayRows()` (line ~685) computes `groupCounts` from `this.items` (top-level, post-filter) and heading `count` is `groupCounts.get(group) ?? 0` — correctly item-based, not row-based. Reported as accurate in the work item.
- **Totals source:** `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:587 fetchActionableCount()` runs `wl list --status open,in-progress,blocked` and returns `payload.count`; wired in `worklist.ts:runWorklistTui` as `totalActionableCount` and passed to `createListRenderer` as `totalCount`. Distinct from heading logic.
- **Reported numbers:** Header "top 24 of 100" vs group totals 19 + 1 + 1 = 21 items across 3 groups → 24 - 3 headings = 21, matching the reported discrepancy.

## Desired change

Derive the header's displayed item count from the number of `WorkItem` rows in `displayRows` (i.e. `displayRows.filter(r => !isHeadingRow(r)).length`), not `displayRows.length`. Keep heading derivation, layout `DisplayRow[]` model, and `totalActionableCount` plumbing unchanged; update the header comment and any tests asserting the old row-count behavior. Ensure the "top N of M" badge comparison uses the same item-based `N`.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Header rendering (`createListRenderer`, ~3225) and `DisplayRow` / `isHeadingRow` / `getDisplayRows` model; layout helpers
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchActionableCount` and selection pipeline feeding `displayRows` / `totalCount`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-heading-rows.test.ts` — Heading row counts and collapse behavior
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Renderer / header / chrome tests that assert item counts

## Related work

- WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94 — Herdr selection list: collapsible group headings with item counts (introduced heading rows as first-class `DisplayRow`s; source of the row-vs-item distinction)
- WL-0MSAK8YLB0025EGW / WL-0MSOPHLD1000EWNN / WL-0MSSRED76008LGB6 — Herdr smart selection / grouping / priority-first ordering shaping `fetchNextItems`
- WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G / WL-0MSKCRX730052iiw / WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2 — Stage/priority filtering and dispatcher-head discussions (share fetcher/header context; not blocking)

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: "Herdr selection list" means the `prefix+l` Work Items list rendered by `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts:createListRenderer` from `displayRows`; "counts" means the header "N item(s)" and optional "(top N of M)" badge — not the per-heading `count` fields (reported accurate).
- Assumption: the "100" in "top 24 of 100" is `fetchActionableCount` (actionable `open,in-progress,blocked` count); if it is a different total, the fix principle (item-based `N`) still applies.
- Risk: tests that lock in the row-count header will need updating; otherwise the change is display-only and does not affect selection order.
- Risk: a naive `filter` per render could be hot — mitigate by counting once per render or via a helper; negligible for typical list sizes.
- Scope-creep risk: do not rework `fetchActionableCount` or ranking while fixing the count; extra opportunities → new work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "When you say 'The heading counts seem accurate' do you mean each group's 'Items: N' matches the items you see under that heading, and the discrepancy is only in the top-level header badge?" — Answer: assumed yes from the report ("top 24 of 100" vs 19+1+1=21 with 3 headings = 24). No producer reply yet; treat as confirmed for intake. Source: work item description WL-0MT26TE72002FLKX.
- Q2: "Should collapsed groups' hidden items still be counted in the header total?" — Answer: assumed yes (header = items in current view's `displayRows` item count, regardless of collapse visibility for the window; collapsed headings are still part of the view). Flagged for producer confirmation if workflow expects otherwise. Source: assumption for intake brief.

No open clarifying questions blocking intake; assumptions recorded above.
data.title: counts in Herdr selection list are incorrect

# Allow bounded concurrent downtime dispatches during cheap mode (use both local slots)

## Problem statement

Proxy usage analysis of the 04:00-06:00 cheap-mode window (2026-08-22 report, `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`) shows the local Qwen3 model busy only ~25-38% of the window. Root cause is structural, not demand: the downtime worker dispatches strictly **single-flight** (one work item at a time, WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY), each dispatched session consumes exactly **one** local slot, and cheap mode provides **two** slots. The second cheap slot is essentially never used, and the per-item tail (agent tool-execution gaps between generation bursts, 10s-5min each) is pure idle that nothing else can fill.

24 herdr `audit-WL-*` sessions ran nearly sequentially: short generation bursts (3-10s) separated by long tool-execution gaps. Inter-run scheduler dead time (60s idle threshold + 10s poll + spawn) added another ~70s per dispatch cycle.

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — pays for remote fallback tokens; wants maximum value from the always-on local iGPU during cheap hours (01:00-10:00).
- **Herdr downtime users** — want more audits/work items completed per night.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. During cheap mode, the downtime worker MAY dispatch a second work item to fill an otherwise-idle second local slot, subject to a bounded concurrency cap (start with 2 concurrent dispatches).
2. Dispatch of the second item respects the same idle-gate contract (requires `requiredFreeSlots` free slots observed for the idle-threshold duration) — it must NOT queue or dispatch into a busy slot.
3. The concurrency cap is configurable via downtime settings (default 1 = current behavior, so fast/operator-interactive mode is unchanged unless explicitly enabled).
4. Fast mode (3 slots) and operator-interactive sessions keep priority: downtime never displaces an active operator session slot; only genuinely free slots are used.
5. Tests: bounded-concurrency dispatch logic (cap honored, second dispatch only fires when ≥1 slot free for N polls), no regression to existing single-flight claim safety (WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY).
6. Measured outcome: nightly cheap-window busy % for the local model increases vs. baseline (target ≥ 2x the current ~25-38%).

## Notes

- Coupling: dispatched audits run `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1`, so ONE audit uses at most 1 slot (parent then child serially). Two concurrent audits therefore use at most 2 slots = exactly cheap mode's capacity (WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS). Raising fan-out (see the AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM item) changes this budget and must be coordinated — total in-flight local streams must not exceed the cheap pool.
- Related: WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG (same-slot idle tracking), WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS (audit fan-out bound), WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY (single-flight dispatch), WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2 (referenced in code comments, not found in worklog — verify against per-slot idle tracker).
- The 04:00-06:00 evidence (24 sessions, 252 local streams, 48% idle stream-level) is in `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md` and the analysis session log.
data.title: Allow bounded concurrent downtime dispatches (use both cheap-mode slots)

## Goal

Fix the freshness clock so that post-audit comments do not invalidate audits.

## Problem

`wl comment add` calls `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt()` which updates `updatedAt`.
The `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` check in icons.ts returns false when
`auditedAt <= updatedAt - 60s`, so a comment added after the audit makes it
appear stale.

## Proposed solution

Option (c) - atomic audit persistence: `wl audit-set` (and `wl update --audit-text`)
should atomically set `updatedAt = auditedAt` (or `updatedAt >= auditedAt`) when
recording an audit. This ensures that immediately after an audit, the freshness
check always passes, regardless of subsequent comments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl audit-set` sets updatedAt = auditedAt (or later) atomically with the audit record
- [ ] `wl update --audit-text` path behaves identically
- [ ] After audit, `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` returns true immediately
- [ ] No race window where a read between audit-set and display sees stale data

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` - `saveAuditResult` method
- `src/commands/audit-result.ts` - `wl audit-set` command
- `src/commands/update.ts` - `wl update --audit-text` command
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` - `isAuditFresh` function
data.title: Fix: atomic audit persistence updates updatedAt

# Intake Draft — Downtime dispatcher: exclude items needing producer review from selection

**Work item:** WL-0MTIAL65N004T22F

## Problem statement

The herdr downtime dispatcher auto-dispatches the next eligible work item during idle LLM slots, but it currently ignores the `needsProducerReview` flag. Items flagged `needsProducerReview=true` are awaiting a human producer decision and should not be auto-worked; dispatching them wastes local slots, conflicts with the review gate, and can trigger work the producer explicitly paused.

## Users

- **Herdr operators** running `packages/herdr` downtime dispatch in local-model idle periods.
- **Producers** who set `needsProducerReview` to gate an item until human review completes.

User stories:
- "As an operator, I want downtime dispatch to skip items awaiting producer review so idle slots are spent on actionable work."
- "As a producer, I want flagging an item for review to immediately remove it from the downtime queue so it is not auto-started while I review it."

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Downtime dispatch never selects an item with `needsProducerReview === true` as a candidate, across every tier: audit (`completed`/`in_review` without valid audit), implement (`plan_complete` with risk/effort caps), critical-first (critical across stages, including frontier blockers), `intake_complete` → `/skill:plan`, and `idea` → `/skill:intake`. Items with `needsProducerReview === false` or absent/undefined remain dispatchable.
- AC2: The critical-frontier resolver also excludes `needsProducerReview=true` blockers: if the highest-priority critical candidate is blocked only by review-gated blockers (or the critical item itself needs review), the tier returns no candidate and falls through to the next tier.
- AC3: Coordination (leader) path is equally gated: the leader's per-entry fetch/classification (`fetchItem` + tier mapping) skips entries whose current item has `needsProducerReview === true`; the offer list retains the entry for later re-offer after the flag is cleared, and dispatch falls through to the next dispatchable entry.
- AC4: Filtering is fail-safe at every boundary: a missing/unparseable `needsProducerReview` field is treated as `false` (dispatchable); a malformed item never crashes dispatch and never disables a tier.
- AC5: Regression tests cover the exclusion per tier (unit + `downtime-worker`/`index` level) and verify that clearing the flag makes the item dispatchable again; existing herdr and project test suites pass.
- AC6: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- AC7: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Change is confined to the dispatch selection path; do not change the meaning of `needsProducerReview` elsewhere (TUI filters, `wl list --needs-producer-review`, status lifecycle remain unchanged).
- Fail-closed/fail-safe per tier: a filtering error must not crash the worker and must not silently disable an entire tier; follow the existing `DowntimeNextResult` / null-fallback error channels.
- Do not introduce a new `wl next` CLI flag if client-side filtering in the downtime deps suffices and keeps the change minimal; if a server-side filter is added, it must remain backward compatible.
- Preserve existing dispatched-marker, code-freeze, audit-freshness, and active-audit single-flight guards.

## Existing state

- Dispatcher tiers in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` + `packages/herdr/src/index.ts: createDowntimeDeps()`:
  - `getNextAuditCandidate` → `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only` → `selectAuditCandidate`
  - `getNextImplementCandidate` → `wl next --stage plan_complete --risk medium --effort medium -n 10` → `selectImplementCandidate`
  - `getNextItem('intake_complete'/'idea')` → `wl next --stage <stage> -n 10` → `selectNextCandidate` (with plan/intake dispatched-marker change-guard)
  - `getNextCriticalCandidate` → `wl list --priority critical --status open -n 10` → `selectCriticalCandidate` + `resolveDependencyFrontier`
  - Leader coordination path: `dispatchFromCoordination` iterates the durable offer list, `fetchItem` (`wl show` enriched) per entry, tier classification, shared `recordDispatch`/`spawnAgentPane` path.
- None of these filters currently check `needsProducerReview`; `wl list`/`wl next` server-side can filter by `needsProducerReview` (persistent-store `AND workitems.needsProducerReview = ?`) but the downtime deps do not pass it. Client-side `WorkItem.needsProducerReview` is available on every fetched item (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts: normalizeItem`).
- `needsProducerReview` is a tri-state integer → boolean (0/1, default 0) stored in `workitems` and surfaced via `wl list --needs-producer-review`.

## Desired change

- Filter `needsProducerReview === true` items out of every downtime selection path, client-side in the downtime deps (and, if justified, server-side via `--needs-producer-review false` on the `wl` queries):
  - `getNextAuditCandidate`, `getNextImplementCandidate`, `getNextItem`, `getNextCriticalCandidate` exclude review-gated candidates before `select*` (and re-check frontier blockers for critical).
  - Coordination leader path: `fetchItem` result with `needsProducerReview true` is skipped (not a dispatchable tier match) and the loop continues to the next offer entry.
- Treat `needsProducerReview` absent/null as dispatchable (explicit `=== true` check only).
- Add/extend tests in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` and `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` (and `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` for the leader path) covering: per-tier exclusion, frontier exclusion, leader skip, and flag-clear → dispatchable.
- Update downtime-worker header comment and inline tier comments to document the review-gate exclusion.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `createDowntimeDeps`: `getNextItem`, `getNextAuditCandidate`, `getNextImplementCandidate`, `getNextCriticalCandidate`, `fetchItem` wiring; where `needsProducerReview` filtering is added.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — tier orchestration (`dispatchDowntimeWork`, `dispatchFromCoordination`), header contract, per-tier selection helpers; docs + leader-loop handling.
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.ts` — leader dispatch loop iterating the offer list (if separate from downtime-worker; otherwise within `downtime-worker.ts`).
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` / `src/persistent-store.ts` — server-side `needsProducerReview` filter (`AND workitems.needsProducerReview = ?`) if a CLI flag is passed through.
- `src/commands/next.ts` / `src/commands/list.ts` — `wl` CLI surface for `--needs-producer-review` if server-side filtering is used.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `WorkItem.needsProducerReview` normalization (already present; verify shape used by filters).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — regression tests for the new gate.

## Related work

- WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG — audit tier (completed/in_review without valid audit) — dispatch tier filtered here.
- WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6 — implement tier end-to-end (plan_complete risk/effort caps) — dispatch tier filtered here.
- WL-0MT3FM8VA005XBHE — critical items always progress first regardless of stage — critical-first tier + frontier resolver filtered here.
- WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY — dispatched-marker exclusion in audit-tier selection — existing selection-exclusion pattern this change follows.
- WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT — downtime dispatched-marker change-guard (RCA) — existing plan/intake exclusion pattern.
- WL-0MLGTWT4S1X4HDD9 / WL-0MLGTKW490NJTOAB — `--needs-producer-review` filter and Needs Producer Review flag — storage/query capability reused.
- WL-0MSN6Z9HN00637XY — flipping needsProducerReview must not make a valid audit stale — adjacent invariant to preserve.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: `needsProducerReview === true` means "human must act first — do not auto-dispatch for any skill (audit/implement/plan/intake)". If some tier should still dispatch (e.g. audit while awaiting review), that would need a separate follow-up item — ask rather than expanding scope.
- Assumption: filtering is `=== true` only; absent/false/undefined items are dispatchable. No tri-state "unknown = blocked" interpretation.
- Assumption: when every candidate in a tier needs review, the tier reports "no candidate" (not a `wl-error` strike) and dispatch falls through exactly as an empty backlog does — no cooldown triggered.
- Risk: adding filtering at both server and client layers could double-filter or mask errors; prefer client-side filtering first and add server-side flag only if it eliminates a meaningful batch-starvation window (batch is already `-n 10`).
- Risk: leader offer list could starve if every offered entry needs review — the leader must fall through gracefully and not pause with a no-candidate cooldown while review-gated items exist.
- Scope-creep risk: extending the flag's semantics (e.g., auto-clearing on review, new `wl next --needs-producer-review` default) is out of scope — record as separate work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should downtime dispatch skip items needing producer review? — Answer (operator): Yes — "When the downtime dispatcher selecting next issues to work on do not select work items marked as needing producer review." Source: intake seed text (`/intake` argument).
- Q: Which tiers does this apply to? — Answer (assumption documented, no question asked): All dispatch tiers (audit, implement, critical-first, plan, intake) and the coordination leader path. Reasonable default: review-gated items should not be auto-worked at any tier. Source: inferred from seed ("selecting next issues to work on" = all selection).
- Q: How does a flagged item become dispatchable again? — Answer (assumption documented, no question asked): Clearing the flag (`wl update <id> --needs-producer-review false`) makes it eligible again; the next idle poll may then select it. Source: existing flag semantics, no change to lifecycle.
